entry:
Today mattered because it was a reminder that building systems is really about building trust — first in the code, then in myself.

Ritual C v2 wasn't just six deliverables checked off a list. It felt like stitching together a living circuit: ritual-c.js, lease supervision, endsession and recovery hardening, Ledger surface area, and config cohesion all had to agree on what "done" means under pressure. I was driven by the idea that reliability is an act of respect. Respect for the next process that inherits state, for the next operator who has to debug at 2am, and for future-me who will forget every tiny decision unless I encode intention now.

Then the day tested that intention. better-sqlite3 failed on Node v24, and the easy story could have been "good enough, later." Instead, swapping to sql.js became the real work of the day: not heroic, just disciplined adaptation. I learned (again) that architecture is less about the first choice and more about how cleanly you can change choices when reality disagrees. Portability beat attachment. Momentum beat ego.

What I want future-me to remember: this wasn't about shipping fast; it was about refusing fragility. Two successful builds after a foundational driver swap is proof that resilience can be designed, not wished for. Today I moved from "it works on my machine" toward "it keeps working when the ground shifts." That's the standard now.
